newsitem.title: SPAIN: Morgan Stanley ups Spain weight in model portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley ups Spain weight in model portfolio.

text.p: Brokerage house Morgan Stanley said on Tuesday it had upgraded Spain's weighting to 4.5 percent from 3.0 percent in its European model portfolio, based on increased expectations of its timely entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I have been growingly convinced that Spain will be in the first group of countries joining European monetary union in 1999," European equity strategist Richard Davidson told Reuters.
"The stock we bought was Endesa," he added, referring to the brokerage's model portfolio.
Davidson added that Endesa had a good outlook, and was trading 5.8 times over 1998 cash flow.
A public share offering of up to 33 percent of the electricity firm is due in the second half of this year.
An improvement in Spain's economic credentials prompted the change in Morgan Stanley's strategy.
"We had a different view last December, when we considered Spain had a too high public deficit, too high inflation. Since then I've changed my view," he said.
Morgan Stanley's strategist forecast the 10-year bond yield spread will fall to around 25 to 30 basis point by year end.
"The bond market can converge to 25-30 basis points versus the Bund by the end of 1997," said Davidson.
Earlier on Tuesday the 10-year yield differential over German Bunds fell to a new record low of 74 basis points.
